# Requirement
```text
 Overall/Domain description.
 Console pipe-connection game: grid with outer walls, one source inside pointing inward, one sink on the border
  pointing outward. Player places pipes from a queue; after a delay, water flows along placed pipes.
Cell[][] uses 0-based array indices, but index 0 and rows-1/cols-1 are occupied by the outer wall border. Therefore, the playable area starts at internal index 1: [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2]. Player-facing coordinates are deliberately aligned with these playable indices: row 1 maps to internal row 1, column 'A' maps to internal col 1. No row-1/col-1 conversion is performed.
 Direction provides four directions plus opposite/offset; PipeShape defines
  connection
  directions; TerminationType distinguishes SOURCE vs SINK.

  Functional Requirements

Coordinate and Direction: Coordinate.row and Coordinate.col represent internal Cell[][] array indices and are used directly as cells[row][col]. A Cell stored at cells[r][c] should have Coordinate(row=r, col=c). 
Because the outer wall border occupies index 0, playable cells naturally start at index 1, so player input aligns with internal playable indices.
  Direction enum provides four directions (UP, DOWN, LEFT, RIGHT) and Pa19Helper provides getOpposite() returning the opposite direction
  and getOffset() returning the unit coordinate offset for movement calculations.

  Game: Operations to place a pipe, skip, undo, advance water flow, check win, check loss; convenience fromString
  constructor; maintain step count. 
Operation placePipe: This method maps the player column letter to an internal column index using col - 'A' + 1, 
keeps row unchanged, and places the pipe at cells[row][colIndex]. For example, placePipe(1, 'A') targets cells[1][1].
Operation skipPipe: Consumes the current pipe from the queue and increments the step count. Operation
  undoStep: Pops the last placed cell from CellStack, restores the pipe to the queue head, clears the cell on the map,
  and increments the step count. Returns false if there are no steps to undo.

  Map: Cells are stored as a 2D array Cell[][] with indices [0..rows-1] × [0..cols-1],
  where index 0 and rows-1/cols-1 are walls (border). The playable area occupies
  internal indices [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2], which aligns with 1-based
  user input mapping. tryPlacePipe(row, col, pipe) accepts playable-area aligned coordinates (row and col in [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2]) and uses them
  directly as array indices (no conversion needed due to the wall alignment).
  It rejects: (1) row/col outside [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2], (2) non-FillableCell,
  or (3) already-occupied cell.

  Cell family: Cell.fromChar parses map chars to concrete cells; FillableCell holds an optional pipe and renders pipe or
  '.'; TerminationCell holds pointingTo direction and Type (SOURCE/SINK), with filled state for rendering; Wall renders
  wall char.

  TerminationCell.toSingleChar: Returns the corresponding arrow character based on the current termination cell's
  filling state and pointingTo direction: when filled, returns the arrow from PipePatterns.Filled; when unfilled,
  returns the arrow from PipePatterns.Unfilled. Both SOURCE and SINK use pointingTo directly without direction reversal.
  Throws IllegalStateException("Invalid pointingTo value!") for unknown direction.

  Pipe: Expose connection directions via getConnections() returning Direction[] based on Shape; char rendering by
  filled/unfilled state; construct from short string code (HZ, VT, TL, TR, BL, BR, CR). getConnections(): Returns the
  list of connection directions based on the current pipe shape; throws IllegalStateException("Unknown shape") if the
  shape is not recognized. toSingleChar(): Returns the character representation of this pipe, different for filled and
  unfilled pipes.

  Water Flow: fillBeginTile() marks the source cell as filled. fillTiles(distance) fills pipes within the specified
  distance from source using BFS-style expansion. Water propagates along pipes only when adjacent pipes have matching
  connection directions (one pipe's direction must be the opposite of the other). Each round increments the fill
  distance by 1.

  Win/Loss Conditions: checkPath() uses BFS to determine if a connected path exists from SOURCE to SINK by following
  (i) from SOURCE, step once in the SOURCE pointingTo direction, and (ii) from a pipe cell, step in each pipe connection direction.
  It does not require the traversed pipes to be filled; reaching the SINK cell implies win. hasLost() returns true when prevFilledTiles == 0,
  meaning no new pipes were filled in the previous round (loss condition). The game checks loss only after delay has ended (distance > 0).

  PipeQueue: peek/consume/undo head pipe and auto-refill to fixed length with random shapes. undo(Pipe) inserts the pipe
  back to the front of the queue.

  DelayBar: countdown() decrements the current value by 1 each round. distance() returns -currentValue, representing how
  far the water should flow (negative during countdown, positive after delay ends).

  CellStack: push/pop last placement; undoCount counts the number of successful undo actions (i.e., successful pop
  operations), not the current stack size; 

  External/Tool Classes (not generated; handwritten or reused,You only need to assume that these Java files mentioned below are already in the pa19 package.)
  Pa19Helper is a small helper/assembly class used to build core game model objects for this project. It provides
  convenience methods to (1) construct a Game by wiring together Map, PipeQueue, DelayBar, and CellStack from given
  inputs, and (2) create/parse basic elements (e.g., Map from a Cell[][] or string representation, map characters/short
  codes into Cell/Pipe). It also centralizes simple direction utilities (opposite direction and unit offsets) used
  during parsing and movement-related calculations.
  Deserializer: Purpose: deserialize map input into runtime objects. Field: Path path (input file path). Constructors:
  Deserializer(String path) delegates to private Deserializer(Path); private Deserializer(Path) validates file existence
  and throws FileNotFoundException if missing. Methods: Game parseGame() reads rows, cols, delay, map lines, and
  optional default pipes, then returns Pa19Helper.createGame(...); on unexpected EOF or I/O failure, returns null
  (and logs error). static Cell[][] parseString(int rows, int cols, String cellsRep) converts multiline text to a Cell
  matrix by character, using Pa19Helper.cellFromChar with SINK type on border cells and SOURCE type on inner
  cells. private String getFirstNonEmptyLine(BufferedReader br) returns the first non-blank, non-comment line (ignores
  lines starting with #), or null at end of stream.

  PipePatterns: Purpose: central constant repository for all map-rendering characters. Design: final utility class with
  private constructor (non-instantiable). Exposed constants: WALL (solid wall block), plus two nested static groups:
  Filled and Unfilled. Each group defines arrow chars (UP_ARROW, DOWN_ARROW, LEFT_ARROW, RIGHT_ARROW) and pipe-shape
  chars (HORIZONTAL, VERTICAL, TOP_LEFT, TOP_RIGHT, BOTTOM_LEFT, BOTTOM_RIGHT, CROSS). Use PipePatterns constants for
  all rendering chars; do not hardcode glyphs in TerminationCell and PipeShape logic.

  StringUtils: Purpose: provide lightweight string helper utilities. Class design: utility class with a private
  constructor to prevent instantiation. 
```

# Task
You will be given a **Requirement**, a **Class Diagram** in PlantUML, and a list of operation specifications. Your task is to correct the specifications that are inconsistent with the requirement.

An operation specification must describe the following sections about the operation:
1. Summary: the summary of functionality;
2. Algorithm: algorithm or pseudo code;
3. Related Features: a list of structural or behavior features within this class that shall be accessed;
4. Related Classes: a list of classes and data types defined in **Class Diagram** that shall be accessed, in the format of `Related Classes: ClsA, CLsB, ...` or `Related Classes: None`;
5. Input: the input parameters, including the meaning, the format, and the value ranges if necessary;
6. Output: output value, including the meaning, the format, and the value ranges if necessary;
7. Pre-condition: the condition that the system and the input must satisfy before the operation is executed;
8. Post-condition: the condition that the system and the output must satisfy after the operation is executed.

Finish this task by following the guidelines below.
1. Read the requirement and the class diagram.

# Requirement
```text
 Overall/Domain description.
 Console pipe-connection game: grid with outer walls, one source inside pointing inward, one sink on the border
  pointing outward. Player places pipes from a queue; after a delay, water flows along placed pipes.
Cell[][] uses 0-based array indices, but index 0 and rows-1/cols-1 are occupied by the outer wall border. Therefore, the playable area starts at internal index 1: [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2]. Player-facing coordinates are deliberately aligned with these playable indices: row 1 maps to internal row 1, column 'A' maps to internal col 1. No row-1/col-1 conversion is performed.
 Direction provides four directions plus opposite/offset; PipeShape defines
  connection
  directions; TerminationType distinguishes SOURCE vs SINK.

  Functional Requirements

Coordinate and Direction: Coordinate.row and Coordinate.col represent internal Cell[][] array indices and are used directly as cells[row][col]. A Cell stored at cells[r][c] should have Coordinate(row=r, col=c). 
Because the outer wall border occupies index 0, playable cells naturally start at index 1, so player input aligns with internal playable indices.
  Direction enum provides four directions (UP, DOWN, LEFT, RIGHT) and Pa19Helper provides getOpposite() returning the opposite direction
  and getOffset() returning the unit coordinate offset for movement calculations.

  Game: Operations to place a pipe, skip, undo, advance water flow, check win, check loss; convenience fromString
  constructor; maintain step count. 
Operation placePipe: This method maps the player column letter to an internal column index using col - 'A' + 1, 
keeps row unchanged, and places the pipe at cells[row][colIndex]. For example, placePipe(1, 'A') targets cells[1][1].
Operation skipPipe: Consumes the current pipe from the queue and increments the step count. Operation
  undoStep: Pops the last placed cell from CellStack, restores the pipe to the queue head, clears the cell on the map,
  and increments the step count. Returns false if there are no steps to undo.

  Map: Cells are stored as a 2D array Cell[][] with indices [0..rows-1] × [0..cols-1],
  where index 0 and rows-1/cols-1 are walls (border). The playable area occupies
  internal indices [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2], which aligns with 1-based
  user input mapping. tryPlacePipe(row, col, pipe) accepts playable-area aligned coordinates (row and col in [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2]) and uses them
  directly as array indices (no conversion needed due to the wall alignment).
  It rejects: (1) row/col outside [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2], (2) non-FillableCell,
  or (3) already-occupied cell.

  Cell family: Cell.fromChar parses map chars to concrete cells; FillableCell holds an optional pipe and renders pipe or
  '.'; TerminationCell holds pointingTo direction and Type (SOURCE/SINK), with filled state for rendering; Wall renders
  wall char.

  TerminationCell.toSingleChar: Returns the corresponding arrow character based on the current termination cell's
  filling state and pointingTo direction: when filled, returns the arrow from PipePatterns.Filled; when unfilled,
  returns the arrow from PipePatterns.Unfilled. Both SOURCE and SINK use pointingTo directly without direction reversal.
  Throws IllegalStateException("Invalid pointingTo value!") for unknown direction.

  Pipe: Expose connection directions via getConnections() returning Direction[] based on Shape; char rendering by
  filled/unfilled state; construct from short string code (HZ, VT, TL, TR, BL, BR, CR). getConnections(): Returns the
  list of connection directions based on the current pipe shape; throws IllegalStateException("Unknown shape") if the
  shape is not recognized. toSingleChar(): Returns the character representation of this pipe, different for filled and
  unfilled pipes.

  Water Flow: fillBeginTile() marks the source cell as filled. fillTiles(distance) fills pipes within the specified
  distance from source using BFS-style expansion. Water propagates along pipes only when adjacent pipes have matching
  connection directions (one pipe's direction must be the opposite of the other). Each round increments the fill
  distance by 1.

  Win/Loss Conditions: checkPath() uses BFS to determine if a connected path exists from SOURCE to SINK by following
  (i) from SOURCE, step once in the SOURCE pointingTo direction, and (ii) from a pipe cell, step in each pipe connection direction.
  It does not require the traversed pipes to be filled; reaching the SINK cell implies win. hasLost() returns true when prevFilledTiles == 0,
  meaning no new pipes were filled in the previous round (loss condition). The game checks loss only after delay has ended (distance > 0).

  PipeQueue: peek/consume/undo head pipe and auto-refill to fixed length with random shapes. undo(Pipe) inserts the pipe
  back to the front of the queue.

  DelayBar: countdown() decrements the current value by 1 each round. distance() returns -currentValue, representing how
  far the water should flow (negative during countdown, positive after delay ends).

  CellStack: push/pop last placement; undoCount counts the number of successful undo actions (i.e., successful pop
  operations), not the current stack size; 

  External/Tool Classes (not generated; handwritten or reused,You only need to assume that these Java files mentioned below are already in the pa19 package.)
  Pa19Helper is a small helper/assembly class used to build core game model objects for this project. It provides
  convenience methods to (1) construct a Game by wiring together Map, PipeQueue, DelayBar, and CellStack from given
  inputs, and (2) create/parse basic elements (e.g., Map from a Cell[][] or string representation, map characters/short
  codes into Cell/Pipe). It also centralizes simple direction utilities (opposite direction and unit offsets) used
  during parsing and movement-related calculations.
  Deserializer: Purpose: deserialize map input into runtime objects. Field: Path path (input file path). Constructors:
  Deserializer(String path) delegates to private Deserializer(Path); private Deserializer(Path) validates file existence
  and throws FileNotFoundException if missing. Methods: Game parseGame() reads rows, cols, delay, map lines, and
  optional default pipes, then returns Pa19Helper.createGame(...); on unexpected EOF or I/O failure, returns null
  (and logs error). static Cell[][] parseString(int rows, int cols, String cellsRep) converts multiline text to a Cell
  matrix by character, using Pa19Helper.cellFromChar with SINK type on border cells and SOURCE type on inner
  cells. private String getFirstNonEmptyLine(BufferedReader br) returns the first non-blank, non-comment line (ignores
  lines starting with #), or null at end of stream.

  PipePatterns: Purpose: central constant repository for all map-rendering characters. Design: final utility class with
  private constructor (non-instantiable). Exposed constants: WALL (solid wall block), plus two nested static groups:
  Filled and Unfilled. Each group defines arrow chars (UP_ARROW, DOWN_ARROW, LEFT_ARROW, RIGHT_ARROW) and pipe-shape
  chars (HORIZONTAL, VERTICAL, TOP_LEFT, TOP_RIGHT, BOTTOM_LEFT, BOTTOM_RIGHT, CROSS). Use PipePatterns constants for
  all rendering chars; do not hardcode glyphs in TerminationCell and PipeShape logic.

  StringUtils: Purpose: provide lightweight string helper utilities. Class design: utility class with a private
  constructor to prevent instantiation. 
```

# Operation Specifications
PipeQueue::undo
Summary:
Restores a pipe to the front of the queue.
Algorithm:
1. Insert the given pipe at the head of the internal queue.
2. If the queue exceeds its configured maximum length, trim or otherwise normalize it according to queue policy.
Related Features:
- pipeQueue: ordered list of upcoming pipes.
- maxGenLength: target queue length.
Related Classes: Pipe
Input:
- pipe: the pipe to be restored to the front of the queue.
Output:
- void.
Pre-condition:
- pipe is not null.
Post-condition:
- pipe becomes the new queue head.
- The queue contents are shifted back by one position.

PipeQueue::generateNewPipe
Summary:
Generates one random pipe and appends it to the queue.
Algorithm:
1. Choose a pipe shape randomly from the supported shapes.
2. Create a new Pipe instance with that shape and an initial unfilled state.
3. Append it to the queue and return it.
Related Features:
- maxGenLength: queue generation policy may constrain usage.
- pipeQueue: storage target for the generated pipe.
Related Classes: Pipe, PipeShape
Input:
- None.
Output:
- Pipe: the newly generated pipe.
Pre-condition:
- PipeQueue has been initialized.
Post-condition:
- The returned pipe is added to the queue.

PipeQueue::peek
Summary:
Returns the current head pipe without removing it.
Algorithm:
1. Read the first pipe in the queue.
2. Return it without modifying the list.
Related Features:
- pipeQueue: ordered list of upcoming pipes.
Related Classes: Pipe
Input:
- None.
Output:
- Pipe: the queue head pipe.
Pre-condition:
- The queue contains at least one pipe.
Post-condition:
- Internal state is unchanged.

PipeQueue::consume
Summary:
Removes the current head pipe from the queue and refreshes the queue if needed.
Algorithm:
1. Remove the first pipe from the internal queue.
2. If the queue length falls below the configured maximum generation length, generate new pipes
   until the queue is refilled to that length.
Related Features:
- pipeQueue: ordered list of upcoming pipes.
- maxGenLength: target length of the queue.
Related Classes: Pipe
Input:
- None.
Output:
- void.
Pre-condition:
- The queue contains at least one pipe.
Post-condition:
- The head pipe is removed.
- The queue length is restored toward the configured fixed length by auto-generated pipes.

2. If the queue exceeds its configured maximum length, trim or otherwise normalize it according to queue policy.

- pipeQueue: ordered list of upcoming pipes.
- maxGenLength: target queue length.
Related Classes: Pipe
Input:
- pipe: the pipe to be restored to the front of the queue.
Output:
- void.
Pre-condition:
- pipe is not null.
Post-condition:
- pipe becomes the new queue head.
- The queue contents are shifted back by one position.

PipeQueue::generateNewPipe
Summary:
Generates one random pipe and appends it to the queue.
Algorithm:
1. Choose a pipe shape randomly from the supported shapes.
2. Create a new Pipe instance with that shape and an initial unfilled state.
3. Append it to the queue and return it.
Related Features:
- maxGenLength: queue generation policy may constrain usage.
- pipeQueue: storage target for the generated pipe.
Related Classes: Pipe, PipeShape
Input:
- None.
Output:
- Pipe: the newly generated pipe.
Pre-condition:
- PipeQueue has been initialized.
Post-condition:
- The returned pipe is added to the queue.

PipeQueue::peek
Summary:
Returns the current head pipe without removing it.
Algorithm:
1. Read the first pipe in the queue.
2. Return it without modifying the list.
Related Features:
- pipeQueue: ordered list of upcoming pipes.
Related Classes: Pipe
Input:
- None.
Output:
- Pipe: the queue head pipe.
Pre-condition:
- The queue contains at least one pipe.
Post-condition:
- Internal state is unchanged.

PipeQueue::consume
Summary:
Removes the current head pipe from the queue and refreshes the queue if needed.
Algorithm:
1. Remove the first pipe from the internal queue.
2. If the queue length falls below the configured maximum generation length, generate new pipes
   until the queue is refilled to that length.
Related Features:
- pipeQueue: ordered list of upcoming pipes.
- maxGenLength: target length of the queue.
Related Classes: Pipe
Input:
- None.
Output:
- void.
Pre-condition:
- The queue contains at least one pipe.
Post-condition:
- The head pipe is removed.
- The queue length is restored toward the configured fixed length by auto-generated pipes.

# Requirement
```text
 Overall/Domain description.
 Console pipe-connection game: grid with outer walls, one source inside pointing inward, one sink on the border
  pointing outward. Player places pipes from a queue; after a delay, water flows along placed pipes.
Cell[][] uses 0-based array indices, but index 0 and rows-1/cols-1 are occupied by the outer wall border. Therefore, the playable area starts at internal index 1: [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2]. Player-facing coordinates are deliberately aligned with these playable indices: row 1 maps to internal row 1, column 'A' maps to internal col 1. No row-1/col-1 conversion is performed.
 Direction provides four directions plus opposite/offset; PipeShape defines
  connection
  directions; TerminationType distinguishes SOURCE vs SINK.

  Functional Requirements

Coordinate and Direction: Coordinate.row and Coordinate.col represent internal Cell[][] array indices and are used directly as cells[row][col]. A Cell stored at cells[r][c] should have Coordinate(row=r, col=c). 
Because the outer wall border occupies index 0, playable cells naturally start at index 1, so player input aligns with internal playable indices.
  Direction enum provides four directions (UP, DOWN, LEFT, RIGHT) and Pa19Helper provides getOpposite() returning the opposite direction
  and getOffset() returning the unit coordinate offset for movement calculations.

  Game: Operations to place a pipe, skip, undo, advance water flow, check win, check loss; convenience fromString
  constructor; maintain step count. 
Operation placePipe: This method maps the player column letter to an internal column index using col - 'A' + 1, 
keeps row unchanged, and places the pipe at cells[row][colIndex]. For example, placePipe(1, 'A') targets cells[1][1].
Operation skipPipe: Consumes the current pipe from the queue and increments the step count. Operation
  undoStep: Pops the last placed cell from CellStack, restores the pipe to the queue head, clears the cell on the map,
  and increments the step count. Returns false if there are no steps to undo.

  Map: Cells are stored as a 2D array Cell[][] with indices [0..rows-1] × [0..cols-1],
  where index 0 and rows-1/cols-1 are walls (border). The playable area occupies
  internal indices [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2], which aligns with 1-based
  user input mapping. tryPlacePipe(row, col, pipe) accepts playable-area aligned coordinates (row and col in [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2]) and uses them
  directly as array indices (no conversion needed due to the wall alignment).
  It rejects: (1) row/col outside [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2], (2) non-FillableCell,
  or (3) already-occupied cell.

  Cell family: Cell.fromChar parses map chars to concrete cells; FillableCell holds an optional pipe and renders pipe or
  '.'; TerminationCell holds pointingTo direction and Type (SOURCE/SINK), with filled state for rendering; Wall renders
  wall char.

  TerminationCell.toSingleChar: Returns the corresponding arrow character based on the current termination cell's
  filling state and pointingTo direction: when filled, returns the arrow from PipePatterns.Filled; when unfilled,
  returns the arrow from PipePatterns.Unfilled. Both SOURCE and SINK use pointingTo directly without direction reversal.
  Throws IllegalStateException("Invalid pointingTo value!") for unknown direction.

  Pipe: Expose connection directions via getConnections() returning Direction[] based on Shape; char rendering by
  filled/unfilled state; construct from short string code (HZ, VT, TL, TR, BL, BR, CR). getConnections(): Returns the
  list of connection directions based on the current pipe shape; throws IllegalStateException("Unknown shape") if the
  shape is not recognized. toSingleChar(): Returns the character representation of this pipe, different for filled and
  unfilled pipes.

  Water Flow: fillBeginTile() marks the source cell as filled. fillTiles(distance) fills pipes within the specified
  distance from source using BFS-style expansion. Water propagates along pipes only when adjacent pipes have matching
  connection directions (one pipe's direction must be the opposite of the other). Each round increments the fill
  distance by 1.

  Win/Loss Conditions: checkPath() uses BFS to determine if a connected path exists from SOURCE to SINK by following
  (i) from SOURCE, step once in the SOURCE pointingTo direction, and (ii) from a pipe cell, step in each pipe connection direction.
  It does not require the traversed pipes to be filled; reaching the SINK cell implies win. hasLost() returns true when prevFilledTiles == 0,
  meaning no new pipes were filled in the previous round (loss condition). The game checks loss only after delay has ended (distance > 0).

  PipeQueue: peek/consume/undo head pipe and auto-refill to fixed length with random shapes. undo(Pipe) inserts the pipe
  back to the front of the queue.

  DelayBar: countdown() decrements the current value by 1 each round. distance() returns -currentValue, representing how
  far the water should flow (negative during countdown, positive after delay ends).

  CellStack: push/pop last placement; undoCount counts the number of successful undo actions (i.e., successful pop
  operations), not the current stack size; 

  External/Tool Classes (not generated; handwritten or reused,You only need to assume that these Java files mentioned below are already in the pa19 package.)
  Pa19Helper is a small helper/assembly class used to build core game model objects for this project. It provides
  convenience methods to (1) construct a Game by wiring together Map, PipeQueue, DelayBar, and CellStack from given
  inputs, and (2) create/parse basic elements (e.g., Map from a Cell[][] or string representation, map characters/short
  codes into Cell/Pipe). It also centralizes simple direction utilities (opposite direction and unit offsets) used
  during parsing and movement-related calculations.
  Deserializer: Purpose: deserialize map input into runtime objects. Field: Path path (input file path). Constructors:
  Deserializer(String path) delegates to private Deserializer(Path); private Deserializer(Path) validates file existence
  and throws FileNotFoundException if missing. Methods: Game parseGame() reads rows, cols, delay, map lines, and
  optional default pipes, then returns Pa19Helper.createGame(...); on unexpected EOF or I/O failure, returns null
  (and logs error). static Cell[][] parseString(int rows, int cols, String cellsRep) converts multiline text to a Cell
  matrix by character, using Pa19Helper.cellFromChar with SINK type on border cells and SOURCE type on inner
  cells. private String getFirstNonEmptyLine(BufferedReader br) returns the first non-blank, non-comment line (ignores
  lines starting with #), or null at end of stream.

  PipePatterns: Purpose: central constant repository for all map-rendering characters. Design: final utility class with
  private constructor (non-instantiable). Exposed constants: WALL (solid wall block), plus two nested static groups:
  Filled and Unfilled. Each group defines arrow chars (UP_ARROW, DOWN_ARROW, LEFT_ARROW, RIGHT_ARROW) and pipe-shape
  chars (HORIZONTAL, VERTICAL, TOP_LEFT, TOP_RIGHT, BOTTOM_LEFT, BOTTOM_RIGHT, CROSS). Use PipePatterns constants for
  all rendering chars; do not hardcode glyphs in TerminationCell and PipeShape logic.

  StringUtils: Purpose: provide lightweight string helper utilities. Class design: utility class with a private
  constructor to prevent instantiation. 
```

# Operation Specifications
Pipe::getConnections
Summary:
Returns the set of directions in which this pipe shape connects.
Algorithm:
1. Inspect the current pipe shape.
2. Return the direction list mapped to that shape:
   - HORIZONTAL -> LEFT, RIGHT
   - VERTICAL -> UP, DOWN
   - TOP_LEFT -> UP, LEFT
   - TOP_RIGHT -> UP, RIGHT
   - BOTTOM_LEFT -> DOWN, LEFT
   - BOTTOM_RIGHT -> DOWN, RIGHT
   - CROSS -> UP, DOWN, LEFT, RIGHT
3. If the shape is unknown, throw IllegalStateException("Unknown shape").
Related Features:
- shape: determines connectivity.
- filled: does not affect connectivity, only rendering.
Related Classes: Direction, PipeShape
Input:
- None.
Output:
- List<Direction>: the connection directions of the pipe shape.
Pre-condition:
- The pipe shape is a recognized PipeShape value.
Post-condition:
- Internal state is unchanged.

# Operation Specifications
Pipe::getConnections
Summary:
Returns the set of directions in which this pipe shape connects.
Algorithm:
1. Inspect the current pipe shape.
2. Return the direction list mapped to that shape:
   - HORIZONTAL -> LEFT, RIGHT
   - VERTICAL -> UP, DOWN
   - TOP_LEFT -> UP, LEFT
   - TOP_RIGHT -> UP, RIGHT
   - BOTTOM_LEFT -> DOWN, LEFT
   - BOTTOM_RIGHT -> DOWN, RIGHT
   - CROSS -> UP, DOWN, LEFT, RIGHT
3. If the shape is unknown, throw IllegalStateException("Unknown shape").
Related Features:
- shape: determines connectivity.
- filled: does not affect connectivity, only rendering.
Related Classes: Direction, PipeShape
Input:
- None.
Output:
- List<Direction>: the connection directions of the pipe shape.
Pre-condition:
- The pipe shape is a recognized PipeShape value.
Post-condition:
- Internal state is unchanged.

# Requirement
```text
 Overall/Domain description.
 Console pipe-connection game: grid with outer walls, one source inside pointing inward, one sink on the border
  pointing outward. Player places pipes from a queue; after a delay, water flows along placed pipes.
Cell[][] uses 0-based array indices, but index 0 and rows-1/cols-1 are occupied by the outer wall border. Therefore, the playable area starts at internal index 1: [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2]. Player-facing coordinates are deliberately aligned with these playable indices: row 1 maps to internal row 1, column 'A' maps to internal col 1. No row-1/col-1 conversion is performed.
 Direction provides four directions plus opposite/offset; PipeShape defines
  connection
  directions; TerminationType distinguishes SOURCE vs SINK.

  Functional Requirements

Coordinate and Direction: Coordinate.row and Coordinate.col represent internal Cell[][] array indices and are used directly as cells[row][col]. A Cell stored at cells[r][c] should have Coordinate(row=r, col=c). 
Because the outer wall border occupies index 0, playable cells naturally start at index 1, so player input aligns with internal playable indices.
  Direction enum provides four directions (UP, DOWN, LEFT, RIGHT) and Pa19Helper provides getOpposite() returning the opposite direction
  and getOffset() returning the unit coordinate offset for movement calculations.

  Game: Operations to place a pipe, skip, undo, advance water flow, check win, check loss; convenience fromString
  constructor; maintain step count. 
Operation placePipe: This method maps the player column letter to an internal column index using col - 'A' + 1, 
keeps row unchanged, and places the pipe at cells[row][colIndex]. For example, placePipe(1, 'A') targets cells[1][1].
Operation skipPipe: Consumes the current pipe from the queue and increments the step count. Operation
  undoStep: Pops the last placed cell from CellStack, restores the pipe to the queue head, clears the cell on the map,
  and increments the step count. Returns false if there are no steps to undo.

  Map: Cells are stored as a 2D array Cell[][] with indices [0..rows-1] × [0..cols-1],
  where index 0 and rows-1/cols-1 are walls (border). The playable area occupies
  internal indices [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2], which aligns with 1-based
  user input mapping. tryPlacePipe(row, col, pipe) accepts playable-area aligned coordinates (row and col in [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2]) and uses them
  directly as array indices (no conversion needed due to the wall alignment).
  It rejects: (1) row/col outside [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2], (2) non-FillableCell,
  or (3) already-occupied cell.

  Cell family: Cell.fromChar parses map chars to concrete cells; FillableCell holds an optional pipe and renders pipe or
  '.'; TerminationCell holds pointingTo direction and Type (SOURCE/SINK), with filled state for rendering; Wall renders
  wall char.

  TerminationCell.toSingleChar: Returns the corresponding arrow character based on the current termination cell's
  filling state and pointingTo direction: when filled, returns the arrow from PipePatterns.Filled; when unfilled,
  returns the arrow from PipePatterns.Unfilled. Both SOURCE and SINK use pointingTo directly without direction reversal.
  Throws IllegalStateException("Invalid pointingTo value!") for unknown direction.

  Pipe: Expose connection directions via getConnections() returning Direction[] based on Shape; char rendering by
  filled/unfilled state; construct from short string code (HZ, VT, TL, TR, BL, BR, CR). getConnections(): Returns the
  list of connection directions based on the current pipe shape; throws IllegalStateException("Unknown shape") if the
  shape is not recognized. toSingleChar(): Returns the character representation of this pipe, different for filled and
  unfilled pipes.

  Water Flow: fillBeginTile() marks the source cell as filled. fillTiles(distance) fills pipes within the specified
  distance from source using BFS-style expansion. Water propagates along pipes only when adjacent pipes have matching
  connection directions (one pipe's direction must be the opposite of the other). Each round increments the fill
  distance by 1.

  Win/Loss Conditions: checkPath() uses BFS to determine if a connected path exists from SOURCE to SINK by following
  (i) from SOURCE, step once in the SOURCE pointingTo direction, and (ii) from a pipe cell, step in each pipe connection direction.
  It does not require the traversed pipes to be filled; reaching the SINK cell implies win. hasLost() returns true when prevFilledTiles == 0,
  meaning no new pipes were filled in the previous round (loss condition). The game checks loss only after delay has ended (distance > 0).

  PipeQueue: peek/consume/undo head pipe and auto-refill to fixed length with random shapes. undo(Pipe) inserts the pipe
  back to the front of the queue.

  DelayBar: countdown() decrements the current value by 1 each round. distance() returns -currentValue, representing how
  far the water should flow (negative during countdown, positive after delay ends).

  CellStack: push/pop last placement; undoCount counts the number of successful undo actions (i.e., successful pop
  operations), not the current stack size; 

  External/Tool Classes (not generated; handwritten or reused,You only need to assume that these Java files mentioned below are already in the pa19 package.)
  Pa19Helper is a small helper/assembly class used to build core game model objects for this project. It provides
  convenience methods to (1) construct a Game by wiring together Map, PipeQueue, DelayBar, and CellStack from given
  inputs, and (2) create/parse basic elements (e.g., Map from a Cell[][] or string representation, map characters/short
  codes into Cell/Pipe). It also centralizes simple direction utilities (opposite direction and unit offsets) used
  during parsing and movement-related calculations.
  Deserializer: Purpose: deserialize map input into runtime objects. Field: Path path (input file path). Constructors:
  Deserializer(String path) delegates to private Deserializer(Path); private Deserializer(Path) validates file existence
  and throws FileNotFoundException if missing. Methods: Game parseGame() reads rows, cols, delay, map lines, and
  optional default pipes, then returns Pa19Helper.createGame(...); on unexpected EOF or I/O failure, returns null
  (and logs error). static Cell[][] parseString(int rows, int cols, String cellsRep) converts multiline text to a Cell
  matrix by character, using Pa19Helper.cellFromChar with SINK type on border cells and SOURCE type on inner
  cells. private String getFirstNonEmptyLine(BufferedReader br) returns the first non-blank, non-comment line (ignores
  lines starting with #), or null at end of stream.

  PipePatterns: Purpose: central constant repository for all map-rendering characters. Design: final utility class with
  private constructor (non-instantiable). Exposed constants: WALL (solid wall block), plus two nested static groups:
  Filled and Unfilled. Each group defines arrow chars (UP_ARROW, DOWN_ARROW, LEFT_ARROW, RIGHT_ARROW) and pipe-shape
  chars (HORIZONTAL, VERTICAL, TOP_LEFT, TOP_RIGHT, BOTTOM_LEFT, BOTTOM_RIGHT, CROSS). Use PipePatterns constants for
  all rendering chars; do not hardcode glyphs in TerminationCell and PipeShape logic.

  StringUtils: Purpose: provide lightweight string helper utilities. Class design: utility class with a private
  constructor to prevent instantiation. 
```

# Operation Specifications
Map::tryPlacePipe
Summary:
Attempts to place a pipe into a fillable playable cell using internal array indices directly.
Algorithm:
1. Verify that row and col are within the playable area [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2].
2. Read cells[row][col] directly.
3. Reject the placement if the target cell is not a FillableCell.
4. Reject the placement if the target FillableCell already contains a pipe.
5. Otherwise store the pipe in the cell and return true.
Related Features:
- cell: 2D grid of map cells.
- rows, cols: boundary checks for playable area.
Related Classes: FillableCell, Pipe, Coordinate
Input:
- row: internal playable row index.
- col: internal playable column index.
- pipe: pipe to be placed.
Output:
- boolean: true if placement succeeded, otherwise false.
Pre-condition:
- Map has been initialized.
- pipe is not null.
- row and col use the playable internal index space.
Post-condition:
- On success, the target FillableCell stores the pipe.
- On failure, the map grid remains unchanged.

Map::hasLost
Summary:
Determines whether the map is in the loss state after a water-flow update.
Algorithm:
1. Check prevFilledTiles from the most recent fill round.
2. Return true when prevFilledTiles == 0, meaning no new pipes were filled in the previous round.
3. Otherwise return false.
Related Features:
- prevFilledTiles: tracks the last round’s new fill count.
- prevFilledDistance: may be used by the map’s flow progression logic.
Related Classes: None
Input:
- None.
Output:
- boolean: true when the previous round filled no new tiles.
Pre-condition:
- The map has already been updated by fillTiles or another fill-related operation.
Post-condition:
- Internal state is unchanged.

Map::undo
Summary:
Clears a previously placed pipe from the given coordinate.
Algorithm:
1. Read the cell at the provided coordinate.
2. If the cell is a FillableCell, remove its stored pipe.
3. Leave all other cells unchanged.
Related Features:
- cell: map grid.
- filledTiles: may be indirectly affected if the implementation also clears fill state.
Related Classes: Coordinate, FillableCell
Input:
- coord: coordinate of the cell to clear, using internal indices.
Output:
- void.
Pre-condition:
- coord refers to an existing cell inside the map grid.
- The target cell is expected to be a fillable cell that previously held a pipe.
Post-condition:
- If the target cell is a FillableCell, its pipe is removed.
- Other map content is unchanged.

Map::fillTiles
Summary:
Fills pipe tiles reachable from the source within a given water-flow distance.
Algorithm:
1. If the source has not been marked filled yet, ensure the beginning tile is filled first.
2. Perform a BFS-style expansion from the set of currently filled tiles.
3. For each candidate neighboring cell:
   a. Ignore coordinates outside the playable area.
   b. Consider only FillableCell instances that contain a pipe.
   c. Check whether the current pipe and neighbor pipe have compatible connection directions
      (one side must connect to the opposite side of the other).
   d. Mark newly reached pipes as filled and record them in filledTiles.
4. Repeat expansion until the requested distance is exhausted.
5. Update prevFilledDistance and prevFilledTiles to reflect the round result.
Related Features:
- cell: the map grid.
- filledTiles: list of currently reached coordinates.
- sourceCell: water origin.
- prevFilledDistance: last processed distance.
- prevFilledTiles: number of tiles filled in the previous round.
Related Classes: Coordinate, FillableCell, Pipe, Direction, TerminationCell
Input:
- distance: non-negative water propagation distance.
Output:
- void.
Pre-condition:
- Map has been initialized.
- The source cell exists.
Post-condition:
- All newly reachable pipe cells within the specified distance are marked filled.
- filledTiles is updated to include the reached coordinates.
- prevFilledTiles reflects the number of newly filled tiles in this invocation.

```text
  far the water should flow (negative during countdown, positive after delay ends).

  CellStack: push/pop last placement; undoCount counts the number of successful undo actions (i.e., successful pop
  operations), not the current stack size; 

  External/Tool Classes (not generated; handwritten or reused,You only need to assume that these Java files mentioned below are already in the pa19 package.)
  Pa19Helper is a small helper/assembly class used to build core game model objects for this project. It provides
  convenience methods to (1) construct a Game by wiring together Map, PipeQueue, DelayBar, and CellStack from given
  inputs, and (2) create/parse basic elements (e.g., Map from a Cell[][] or string representation, map characters/short
  codes into Cell/Pipe). It also centralizes simple direction utilities (opposite direction and unit offsets) used
  during parsing and movement-related calculations.
  Deserializer: Purpose: deserialize map input into runtime objects. Field: Path path (input file path). Constructors:
  Deserializer(String path) delegates to private Deserializer(Path); private Deserializer(Path) validates file existence
  and throws FileNotFoundException if missing. Methods: Game parseGame() reads rows, cols, delay, map lines, and
  optional default pipes, then returns Pa19Helper.createGame(...); on unexpected EOF or I/O failure, returns null
  (and logs error). static Cell[][] parseString(int rows, int cols, String cellsRep) converts multiline text to a Cell
  matrix by character, using Pa19Helper.cellFromChar with SINK type on border cells and SOURCE type on inner
  cells. private String getFirstNonEmptyLine(BufferedReader br) returns the first non-blank, non-comment line (ignores
  lines starting with #), or null at end of stream.

  PipePatterns: Purpose: central constant repository for all map-rendering characters. Design: final utility class with
  private constructor (non-instantiable). Exposed constants: WALL (solid wall block), plus two nested static groups:
  Filled and Unfilled. Each group defines arrow chars (UP_ARROW, DOWN_ARROW, LEFT_ARROW, RIGHT_ARROW) and pipe-shape
  chars (HORIZONTAL, VERTICAL, TOP_LEFT, TOP_RIGHT, BOTTOM_LEFT, BOTTOM_RIGHT, CROSS). Use PipePatterns constants for
  all rendering chars; do not hardcode glyphs in TerminationCell and PipeShape logic.

  StringUtils: Purpose: provide lightweight string helper utilities. Class design: utility class with a private
  constructor to prevent instantiation. 
```

# Operation Specifications
Map::tryPlacePipe
Summary:
Attempts to place a pipe into a fillable playable cell using internal array indices directly.
Algorithm:
1. Verify that row and col are within the playable area [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2].
2. Read cells[row][col] directly.
3. Reject the placement if the target cell is not a FillableCell.
4. Reject the placement if the target FillableCell already contains a pipe.
5. Otherwise store the pipe in the cell and return true.
Related Features:
- cell: 2D grid of map cells.
- rows, cols: boundary checks for playable area.
Related Classes: FillableCell, Pipe, Coordinate
Input:
- row: internal playable row index.
- col: internal playable column index.
- pipe: pipe to be placed.
Output:
- boolean: true if placement succeeded, otherwise false.
Pre-condition:
- Map has been initialized.
- pipe is not null.
- row and col use the playable internal index space.
Post-condition:
- On success, the target FillableCell stores the pipe.
- On failure, the map grid remains unchanged.

Map::hasLost
Summary:
Determines whether the map is in the loss state after a water-flow update.
Algorithm:
1. Check prevFilledTiles from the most recent fill round.
2. Return true when prevFilledTiles == 0, meaning no new pipes were filled in the previous round.
3. Otherwise return false.
Related Features:
- prevFilledTiles: tracks the last round’s new fill count.
- prevFilledDistance: may be used by the map’s flow progression logic.
Related Classes: None
Input:
- None.
Output:
- boolean: true when the previous round filled no new tiles.
Pre-condition:
- The map has already been updated by fillTiles or another fill-related operation.
Post-condition:
- Internal state is unchanged.

Map::undo
Summary:
Clears a previously placed pipe from the given coordinate.
Algorithm:
1. Read the cell at the provided coordinate.
2. If the cell is a FillableCell, remove its stored pipe.
3. Leave all other cells unchanged.
Related Features:
- cell: map grid.
- filledTiles: may be indirectly affected if the implementation also clears fill state.
Related Classes: Coordinate, FillableCell
Input:
- coord: coordinate of the cell to clear, using internal indices.
Output:
- void.
Pre-condition:
- coord refers to an existing cell inside the map grid.
- The target cell is expected to be a fillable cell that previously held a pipe.
Post-condition:
- If the target cell is a FillableCell, its pipe is removed.
- Other map content is unchanged.

Map::fillTiles
Summary:
Fills pipe tiles reachable from the source within a given water-flow distance.
Algorithm:
1. If the source has not been marked filled yet, ensure the beginning tile is filled first.
2. Perform a BFS-style expansion from the set of currently filled tiles.
3. For each candidate neighboring cell:
   a. Ignore coordinates outside the playable area.
   b. Consider only FillableCell instances that contain a pipe.
   c. Check whether the current pipe and neighbor pipe have compatible connection directions
      (one side must connect to the opposite side of the other).
   d. Mark newly reached pipes as filled and record them in filledTiles.
4. Repeat expansion until the requested distance is exhausted.
5. Update prevFilledDistance and prevFilledTiles to reflect the round result.
Related Features:
- cell: the map grid.
- filledTiles: list of currently reached coordinates.
- sourceCell: water origin.
- prevFilledDistance: last processed distance.
- prevFilledTiles: number of tiles filled in the previous round.
Related Classes: Coordinate, FillableCell, Pipe, Direction, TerminationCell
Input:
- distance: non-negative water propagation distance.
Output:
- void.
Pre-condition:
- Map has been initialized.
- The source cell exists.
Post-condition:
- All newly reachable pipe cells within the specified distance are marked filled.
- filledTiles is updated to include the reached coordinates.
- prevFilledTiles reflects the number of newly filled tiles in this invocation.

   * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
   * <!-- end-user-doc -->
   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
   * Summary:
   * Places the current pipe from the queue onto the map at the specified player-facing coordinate.
   * Algorithm:
   * 1. Convert the input column letter to an internal column index using col - 'A' + 1.
   * 2. Keep the row unchanged because player-facing rows already align with internal indices.
   * 3. Peek the current pipe from the queue.
   * 4. Attempt to place that pipe at the map cell identified by the converted coordinates.
   * 5. If placement succeeds:
   *    a. Push the placed cell onto the CellStack.
   *    b. Consume the pipe from the queue.
   *    c. Increment the step count.
   *    d. Return true.
   * 6. If placement fails, return false without consuming the pipe.
   * Related Features:
   * - numOfSteps: increments on successful placement.
   * - cellStack: records successful placements for undo.
   * - map: receives the placement request.
   * - pipeQueue: supplies the current pipe.
   * Related Classes: CellStack, Map, PipeQueue, Pipe
   * Input:
   * - row: playable row coordinate, aligned with internal indices, typically in [1..rows-2].
   * - col: player-facing column letter, where 'A' maps to internal column 1.
   * Output:
   * - boolean: true if the pipe was successfully placed, otherwise false.
   * Pre-condition:
   * - Game has been initialized.
   * - The queue contains at least one pipe.
   * - The provided row/column refer to a valid playable cell.
   * Post-condition:
   * - On success, the target map cell contains the placed pipe.
   * - On success, the placed cell is recorded in the stack.
   * - On success, the queue head advances to the next pipe.
   * - numOfSteps increases by 1 only on success.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public boolean placePipe(final int row, final char col)
  {
    int internalCol = col - 'A' + 1;
    Pipe currentPipe = getPipeQueue().peek();
    boolean success = getMap().tryPlacePipe(row, internalCol, currentPipe);
    if (success)
    {
      FillableCell placedCell = (FillableCell)getMap().getCell()[row][internalCol];
      getCellStack().push(placedCell);
      getPipeQueue().consume();
      setNumOfSteps(getNumOfSteps() + 1);
      return true;
    }
    return false;
    
  }

  /**
   * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
   * <!-- end-user-doc -->
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
   * Summary:

   * Algorithm:

  }

  /**
   * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
   * <!-- end-user-doc -->
   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
   * Summary:
   * Undoes the most recent successful pipe placement.
   * Algorithm:
   * 1. If the CellStack has no placed cell to undo, return false.
   * 2. Pop the latest placed FillableCell from the CellStack.
   * 3. Restore that pipe to the front of the PipeQueue using undo(pipe).
   * 4. Clear the corresponding map cell using map.undo(coord).
   * 5. Increment the step count.
   * 6. Return true.
   * Related Features:
   * - cellStack: stores placement history.
   * - pipeQueue: receives the restored pipe.
   * - map: clears the previously occupied cell.
   * - numOfSteps: increments on successful undo.
   * Related Classes: CellStack, PipeQueue, Map, FillableCell, Pipe
   * Input:
   * - None.
   * Output:
   * - boolean: true if an undo was performed, false if there is nothing to undo.
   * Pre-condition:
   * - Game has been initialized.
   * Post-condition:
   * - On success, the last placed pipe is removed from the map.
   * - On success, the removed pipe is returned to the queue head.
   * - On success, the stack size decreases by 1 and undo count increases by 1.
   * - numOfSteps increases by 1 only when undo succeeds.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public boolean undoStep()
  {
    if (getCellStack().getCount() <= 0)
    {
      return false;
    }
    FillableCell cell = getCellStack().pop();
    getPipeQueue().undo(cell.getPipe());
    getMap().undo(new Coordinate() {{ setRow(cell.getRow()); setCol(cell.getCol()); }});
    setNumOfSteps(getNumOfSteps() + 1);
    return true;
    
  }

  /**
   * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
   * <!-- end-user-doc -->
   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
   * Summary:
   * Advances the game by one time step and updates the water-flow state.
   * Algorithm:
   * 1. Decrement the delay bar by one round.
   * 2. Query the current flow distance from the delay bar.
   * 3. If the distance is greater than 0:
   *    a. Fill the source beginning tile.
   *    b. Propagate water through pipes up to the current flow distance.
   *    c. Update map state such as previous filled tile count/distance.
   * 4. If the distance is not greater than 0, do not propagate water.
   * Related Features:

   * - map: performs filling and connectivity updates.

   * Input:

   * - If water-flow has started, map fill state may change.
   * - Previous fill metadata in the map is updated consistently with the latest round.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public void updateState()

    }
    
  }

          FillableCell currentCell = (FillableCell)getCell()[row][col];
          FillableCell neighbor = (FillableCell)neighborCell;
          Pipe currentPipe = currentCell.getPipe();
          Pipe neighborPipe = neighbor.getPipe();
          if (currentPipe == null || neighborPipe == null || neighborPipe.isFilled())
          {
            continue;
          }
          Direction fromDir = null;
          Direction toDir = null;
          if (delta[0] == -1)
          {
            fromDir = Direction.UP;
            toDir = Direction.DOWN;
          }
          else if (delta[0] == 1)
          {
            fromDir = Direction.DOWN;
            toDir = Direction.UP;
          }
          else if (delta[1] == -1)
          {
            fromDir = Direction.LEFT;
            toDir = Direction.RIGHT;
          }
          else if (delta[1] == 1)
          {
            fromDir = Direction.RIGHT;
            toDir = Direction.LEFT;
          }
          if (currentPipe.getConnections().contains(fromDir) && neighborPipe.getConnections().contains(toDir))
          {
            neighborPipe.setFilled(true);
            Coordinate newCoord = Pa19Factory.eINSTANCE.createCoordinate();
            newCoord.setRow(nr);
            newCoord.setCol(nc);
            getFilledTiles().add(newCoord);
            nextFrontier.add(newCoord);
            newlyFilled++;
          }
        }
      }
      frontier = nextFrontier;
    }

    setPrevFilledDistance(distance);
    setPrevFilledTiles(newlyFilled);
    
  }

  public boolean checkPath()
  { ... /* omitted */ }

  /**
   * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
   * <!-- end-user-doc -->
   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->

   * Determines whether the map is in the loss state after water-flow progression has ended.
   * Algorithm:

```java
   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
   * Summary:
```
```java
   * Fills pipe tiles reachable from the source within a given water-flow distance.
   * Algorithm:
   * 1. If the source has not been marked filled yet, ensure the beginning tile is filled first.
   * 2. Perform a BFS-style expansion from the set of currently filled tiles.
   * 3. For each candidate neighboring cell:
   *    a. Ignore coordinates outside the playable area.
   *    b. Consider only FillableCell instances that contain a pipe.
   *    c. Check whether the current pipe and neighbor pipe have compatible connection directions
   *       (one side must connect to the opposite side of the other).
   *    d. Mark newly reached pipes as filled and record them in filledTiles.
   * 4. Repeat expansion until the requested distance is exhausted.
   * 5. Update prevFilledDistance and prevFilledTiles to reflect the round result.
   * Related Features:
   * - cell: the map grid.
   * - filledTiles: list of currently reached coordinates.
   * - sourceCell: water origin.
   * - prevFilledDistance: last processed distance.
   * - prevFilledTiles: number of tiles filled in the previous round.
   * Related Classes: Coordinate, FillableCell, Pipe, Direction, TerminationCell
   * Input:
   * - distance: water propagation distance; may be zero or positive.
   * Output:
   * - void.
   * Pre-condition:
   * - Map has been initialized.
   * - The source cell exists.
   * - distance is non-negative.
   * Post-condition:
   * - All newly reachable pipe cells within the specified distance are marked filled.
   * - filledTiles is updated to include the reached coordinates.
   * - prevFilledTiles reflects the number of newly filled tiles in this invocation.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public void fillTiles(final int distance)
  {
    if (!getSourceCell().isFilled())
    {
      fillBeginTile();
    }

    int newlyFilled = 0;
    EList<Coordinate> frontier = new org.eclipse.emf.common.util.BasicEList<Coordinate>();
    frontier.addAll(getFilledTiles());

    int remaining = distance;
    while (remaining-- > 0 && !frontier.isEmpty())
    {
      EList<Coordinate> nextFrontier = new org.eclipse.emf.common.util.BasicEList<Coordinate>();
      for (Coordinate coord : frontier)
      {
        int row = coord.getRow();
        int col = coord.getCol();
        int[][] deltas = new int[][] { { -1, 0 }, { 1, 0 }, { 0, -1 }, { 0, 1 } };
        for (int[] delta : deltas)
        {
          int nr = row + delta[0];
          int nc = col + delta[1];
          if (nr < 1 || nr > getRows() - 2 || nc < 1 || nc > getCols() - 2)
          {
            continue;
          }
          Cell neighborCell = getCell()[nr][nc];
          if (!(neighborCell instanceof FillableCell))
          {
            continue;
          }
          FillableCell currentCell = (FillableCell)getCell()[row][col];
          FillableCell neighbor = (FillableCell)neighborCell;
          Pipe currentPipe = currentCell.getPipe();
          Pipe neighborPipe = neighbor.getPipe();
          if (currentPipe == null || neighborPipe == null || neighborPipe.isFilled())
          {
            continue;
          }
          Direction fromDir = null;
          Direction toDir = null;
          if (delta[0] == -1)
          {
            fromDir = Direction.UP;
            toDir = Direction.DOWN;
          }
          else if (delta[0] == 1)
          {
            fromDir = Direction.DOWN;
            toDir = Direction.UP;
          }
          else if (delta[1] == -1)
          {
            fromDir = Direction.LEFT;
            toDir = Direction.RIGHT;
          }
          else if (delta[1] == 1)
          {
            fromDir = Direction.RIGHT;
            toDir = Direction.LEFT;
          }
          if (currentPipe.getConnections().contains(fromDir) && neighborPipe.getConnections().contains(toDir))
          {
            neighborPipe.setFilled(true);
            Coordinate newCoord = Pa19Factory.eINSTANCE.createCoordinate();
            newCoord.setRow(nr);
            newCoord.setCol(nc);
            getFilledTiles().add(newCoord);
            nextFrontier.add(newCoord);
            newlyFilled++;
          }
        }
      }
      frontier = nextFrontier;
    }

    setPrevFilledDistance(distance);
    setPrevFilledTiles(newlyFilled);
    
  }
```

```java
   * 2. Perform a BFS-style expansion from the set of currently filled tiles.
   * 3. For each candidate neighboring cell:
   *    a. Ignore coordinates outside the playable area.
   *    b. Consider only FillableCell instances that contain a pipe.
   *    c. Check whether the current pipe and neighbor pipe have compatible connection directions
   *       (one side must connect to the opposite side of the other).
   *    d. Mark newly reached pipes as filled and record them in filledTiles.
   * 4. Repeat expansion until the requested distance is exhausted.
   * 5. Update prevFilledDistance and prevFilledTiles to reflect the round result.
   * Related Features:
   * - cell: the map grid.
   * - filledTiles: list of currently reached coordinates.
   * - sourceCell: water origin.
   * - prevFilledDistance: last processed distance.
   * - prevFilledTiles: number of tiles filled in the previous round.
   * Related Classes: Coordinate, FillableCell, Pipe, Direction, TerminationCell
   * Input:

   * Output:
   * - void.
   * Pre-condition:

  public void fillTiles(final int distance)
  {
    if (!getSourceCell().isFilled())
    {
      fillBeginTile();
    }

    int newlyFilled = 0;
    EList<Coordinate> frontier = new org.eclipse.emf.common.util.BasicEList<Coordinate>();
    frontier.addAll(getFilledTiles());

    int remaining = distance;
    while (remaining-- > 0 && !frontier.isEmpty())
    {
      EList<Coordinate> nextFrontier = new org.eclipse.emf.common.util.BasicEList<Coordinate>();
      for (Coordinate coord : frontier)
      {
        int row = coord.getRow();
        int col = coord.getCol();
        int[][] deltas = new int[][] { { -1, 0 }, { 1, 0 }, { 0, -1 }, { 0, 1 } };
        for (int[] delta : deltas)
        {
          int nr = row + delta[0];
          int nc = col + delta[1];
          if (nr < 1 || nr > getRows() - 2 || nc < 1 || nc > getCols() - 2)
          {
            continue;
          }
          Cell neighborCell = getCell()[nr][nc];
          if (!(neighborCell instanceof FillableCell))
          {
            continue;
          }
          FillableCell currentCell = (FillableCell)getCell()[row][col];
          FillableCell neighbor = (FillableCell)neighborCell;
          Pipe currentPipe = currentCell.getPipe();
          Pipe neighborPipe = neighbor.getPipe();
          if (currentPipe == null || neighborPipe == null || neighborPipe.isFilled())
          {
            continue;
          }
          Direction fromDir = null;
          Direction toDir = null;
          if (delta[0] == -1)
          {
            fromDir = Direction.UP;
            toDir = Direction.DOWN;
          }
          else if (delta[0] == 1)
          {
            fromDir = Direction.DOWN;
            toDir = Direction.UP;
          }
          else if (delta[1] == -1)
          {
            fromDir = Direction.LEFT;
            toDir = Direction.RIGHT;
          }
          else if (delta[1] == 1)
          {
            fromDir = Direction.RIGHT;
            toDir = Direction.LEFT;
          }
          if (currentPipe.getConnections().contains(fromDir) && neighborPipe.getConnections().contains(toDir))
          {
            neighborPipe.setFilled(true);
            Coordinate newCoord = Pa19Factory.eINSTANCE.createCoordinate();
            newCoord.setRow(nr);
            newCoord.setCol(nc);
            getFilledTiles().add(newCoord);
            nextFrontier.add(newCoord);
            newlyFilled++;
          }
        }
      }
      frontier = nextFrontier;
    }

    setPrevFilledDistance(distance);
    setPrevFilledTiles(newlyFilled);
    
  }
```

```java
    EList<Coordinate> frontier = new org.eclipse.emf.common.util.BasicEList<Coordinate>();
    frontier.addAll(getFilledTiles());

    int remaining = distance;
    while (remaining-- > 0 && !frontier.isEmpty())
    {
      EList<Coordinate> nextFrontier = new org.eclipse.emf.common.util.BasicEList<Coordinate>();
      for (Coordinate coord : frontier)
      {
        int row = coord.getRow();
        int col = coord.getCol();
        int[][] deltas = new int[][] { { -1, 0 }, { 1, 0 }, { 0, -1 }, { 0, 1 } };
        for (int[] delta : deltas)
        {
          int nr = row + delta[0];
          int nc = col + delta[1];
          if (nr < 1 || nr > getRows() - 2 || nc < 1 || nc > getCols() - 2)
          {
            continue;
          }
          Cell neighborCell = getCell()[nr][nc];
          if (!(neighborCell instanceof FillableCell))
          {
            continue;
          }
          FillableCell currentCell = (FillableCell)getCell()[row][col];
          FillableCell neighbor = (FillableCell)neighborCell;
          Pipe currentPipe = currentCell.getPipe();
          Pipe neighborPipe = neighbor.getPipe();
          if (currentPipe == null || neighborPipe == null || neighborPipe.isFilled())
          {
            continue;
          }
          Direction fromDir = null;
          Direction toDir = null;
          if (delta[0] == -1)
          {
            fromDir = Direction.UP;
            toDir = Direction.DOWN;
          }
          else if (delta[0] == 1)
          {
            fromDir = Direction.DOWN;
            toDir = Direction.UP;
          }
          else if (delta[1] == -1)
          {
            fromDir = Direction.LEFT;
            toDir = Direction.RIGHT;
          }
          else if (delta[1] == 1)
          {
            fromDir = Direction.RIGHT;
            toDir = Direction.LEFT;
          }
          if (currentPipe.getConnections().contains(fromDir) && neighborPipe.getConnections().contains(toDir))
          {
            neighborPipe.setFilled(true);
            Coordinate newCoord = Pa19Factory.eINSTANCE.createCoordinate();
            newCoord.setRow(nr);
            newCoord.setCol(nc);
            getFilledTiles().add(newCoord);
            nextFrontier.add(newCoord);
            newlyFilled++;
          }
        }
      }
      frontier = nextFrontier;
    }

    setPrevFilledDistance(distance);
    setPrevFilledTiles(newlyFilled);
    
  }
```

```java
            fromDir = Direction.UP;
            toDir = Direction.DOWN;
          }
          else if (delta[0] == 1)
          {
            fromDir = Direction.DOWN;
            toDir = Direction.UP;
          }
          else if (delta[1] == -1)
          {
            fromDir = Direction.LEFT;
            toDir = Direction.RIGHT;
          }
          else if (delta[1] == 1)
          {
            fromDir = Direction.RIGHT;
            toDir = Direction.LEFT;
          }
          if (currentPipe.getConnections().contains(fromDir) && neighborPipe.getConnections().contains(toDir))
          {
            neighborPipe.setFilled(true);
            Coordinate newCoord = Pa19Factory.eINSTANCE.createCoordinate();
            newCoord.setRow(nr);
            newCoord.setCol(nc);
            getFilledTiles().add(newCoord);
            nextFrontier.add(newCoord);
            newlyFilled++;
          }
        }
      }
      frontier = nextFrontier;
    }

    setPrevFilledDistance(distance);
    setPrevFilledTiles(newlyFilled);
    
  }
```

            fromDir = Direction.LEFT;
            toDir = Direction.RIGHT;
          }
          else if (delta[1] == 1)
          {
            fromDir = Direction.RIGHT;
            toDir = Direction.LEFT;
          }
          if (currentPipe.getConnections().contains(fromDir) && neighborPipe.getConnections().contains(toDir))
          {
            neighborPipe.setFilled(true);
            Coordinate newCoord = Pa19Factory.eINSTANCE.createCoordinate();
            newCoord.setRow(nr);
            newCoord.setCol(nc);
            getFilledTiles().add(newCoord);
            nextFrontier.add(newCoord);
            newlyFilled++;
          }
        }
      }
      frontier = nextFrontier;
    }

    setPrevFilledDistance(distance);
    setPrevFilledTiles(newlyFilled);
